summary: EtherNet/IP module reaches T2 across multiple critical findings: pccc_supported (class 0x67 answered → PCCC read/write reachable on MicroLogix/SLC → password hash pull is one packet away), reset_service_capable (Identity Object accepts GetAttrsAll → service 0x05 Reset is exposed on the same session, unauth CPU stop is one packet away), file_object_supported (class 0x37 instance 0xC8 → firmware download slot reachable). Also strong stance findings (unauth_session, cip_security_off) and rich fingerprint (TCPIP object → hostname/domain/DNS, EthLink → MAC). Gap: never actually issues PCCC read or File Object upload even as safe canary — could pull PCCC password hash on MicroLogix without hurting anything.

findings.title_pattern: EtherNet/IP Class 1 implicit I/O exposed on UDP/2222
findings.tier_evidence: UDP/2222 open is deterministic evidence of Class 1 implicit I/O on the segment.
findings.promotion_notes: Passive capture: tcpdump on 2222/udp for N seconds; parse assemblies to prove sensor values are readable/forgeable → T2 evidence of the exposure.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -ni any -w /tmp/enip-io.pcap udp port 2222 and host <ip>; parse with cip-dissector; identify assemblies. Injection PoC is lab-only.

findings.title_pattern: EtherNet/IP device reachable on scanned network
findings.tier_evidence: List Identity returned a valid CIP Identity item — deterministic ENIP fingerprint.

findings.title_pattern: EtherNet/IP identity disclosed (vendor / product / firmware / serial)
findings.promotion_notes: Already partly promoted via enip_known_cve; keep this informational.
findings.tester_next_step: Look up vendor_id + product_code + revision on the Rockwell/Schneider/Omron support portals for firmware CVE bands.

findings.tier_evidence: RegisterSession returned a real session handle — deterministic policy failure.
findings.promotion_notes: T2 evidence is provided by the follow-on unauth GetAttrsAll on Identity/TCPIP/EthLink/PCCC/File classes — any of them succeeding on this session IS the proof-of-primitive.
findings.tester_next_step: python -m cpppo.server.enip.client --address <ip> --print --route-path 1/0 (backplane walk); if session accepts explicit messaging, enumerate all classes.

findings.title_pattern: CIP Security disabled — plaintext explicit messaging accepted
findings.tier_evidence: Plaintext RegisterSession on 44818 succeeded → CIP Security Confidentiality Profile not enforced.
findings.promotion_notes: Posture — no further probe available beyond the port 2221 co-presence check.
findings.tester_next_step: nmap -p 2221,44818 <ip> — if 2221 is also open, CIP Security is available but not enforced (worse); if 2221 is closed, firmware may not support it.

findings.title_pattern: CIP TCP/IP Interface Object exposes hostname / domain / DNS
findings.tier_evidence: Class 0xF5 GetAttrsAll returns actual hostname/domain/DNS/gateway strings from the device — deterministic disclosure.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed hostname/domain into AD/DNS correlation; internal DNS reachability is a segmentation finding — probe listed DNS servers with dig ANY from same segment.
findings.tester_next_step: python -m cpppo.server.enip.client --address <ip> --print '@0xF5/1'; dig ANY <domain_name> @<name_server_1>; identify AD forest / internal namespace exposed to OT.

findings.title_pattern: CIP Ethernet Link Object exposes MAC address
findings.tier_evidence: Class 0xF6 GetAttrsAll — protocol-exposed MAC. Not a vuln.
findings.promotion_notes: MAC is the reference for asset inventory; feeds known_ot_assets.
findings.tester_next_step: Cross-reference MAC OUI against IEEE registry (Rockwell 00:00:BC / Siemens 00:1B:1B / etc); correlate with ARP/DHCP scans on the same segment.
Note the cip_encapsulation flag — if clear, RegisterSession will fail even though the port answered.

findings.title_pattern: EtherNet/IP bridge / gateway detected (List Interfaces populated)
findings.tier_evidence: Non-CIP interface items in List Interfaces reply — deterministic bridge/chassis indicator.
findings.promotion_notes: Walk the backplane via ForwardOpen with padded EPATHs to enumerate downstream modules — safe if only reads; also see enip_backplane_enum.
findings.tester_next_step: python -m cpppo.server.enip.client --address <ip> --route-path 1/0 --print (slot 0 CPU); repeat with --route-path 1/1, 1/2, ... to enumerate every module on the chassis backplane.

findings.title_pattern: CIP backplane routable — ForwardOpen accepted by Connection Manager
findings.tier_evidence: Class 0x06 answered GetAttrsAll — Connection Manager present, ForwardOpen routing is capability. Not proof of a successful ForwardOpen.
findings.promotion_notes: Actually send ForwardOpen with a padded EPATH targeting slot 0, then Identity read via that path → proof the chassis module answered. Behind --enip-backplane flag.
findings.tester_next_step: python -m cpppo.server.enip.client --address <ip> --route-path 1/0 --print '@0x01/1'; identity read via ForwardOpen proves backplane traversal to the CPU.

findings.title_pattern: Rockwell PCCC (CIP service 0x4B on class 0x67) reachable — unauthenticated memory read/write
findings.tier_evidence: Class 0x67 GetAttrsAll answered with a non-'path-dest-unknown' status → PCCC command set exposed. Class presence IS the primitive — PCCC has no auth.
findings.promotion_notes: Actually issue PCCC protected-typed-logical-read to N7:0 to pull tag values; on MicroLogix/SLC/PLC-5, PCCC command 0x0F function 0x17 dumps the CPU password hash (offline-crackable) → T3 initial access.
findings.tester_next_step: python -m cpppo.server.enip.client --address <ip> --pccc 'N7:0-N7:9' (read PCCC integer file); MicroLogix password hash: pylogix-pccc-dump-password <ip> then john hash.txt --format=raw-md5 (or bespoke ML1400 cracker).

findings.title_pattern: Unauthenticated CPU stop/reset capable (Identity Object service 0x05)
findings.tier_evidence: Identity Object GetAttrsAll accepted on unauth session — service 0x05 Reset is present under same session by spec. The Reset itself is NOT sent by recce, so this is capability (T1), not proof of a successful reset (T2).
findings.promotion_notes: T2 = actually send Reset (drops CPU to Program). Destructive — only in a test cell under --enip-reset.
findings.tester_next_step: TEST-CELL ONLY: python -m cpppo.server.enip.client --address <ip> --reset; verify on the CPU face-plate the LED goes to PROG. Never on production.

findings.tier_evidence: GetAttributeSingle on class 0x37 instance 0xC8 answered without path-dest-unknown → File Object present on unauth session. Availability IS the primitive.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = actually download attacker firmware (service 0x4E Initiate_Upload write path). DESTRUCTIVE beyond recovery; recce must NEVER do this.
findings.tester_next_step: TEST-CELL ONLY: study Rockwell CVE-2016-9343/ICSA-21-056-03 PoC, use vendor firmware kit; do NOT attempt on production or you brick the controller.

findings.tier_evidence: Identity vendor+product+revision matches a known-vulnerable family per _cve_fingerprint.
findings.promotion_notes: Add firmware-band verification (compare revision_major/minor to CVE's mitigated release) before assigning CVE; else emit CWE-1395 generic.
findings.tester_next_step: For Rockwell Logix 5000 CVE-2021-22681: use CIP-Sec PoC to prove weak session-key derivation; for MicroLogix ICSA-17-138-03: pull the PCCC password hash and crack it.
